previous_entry: Once a prosperous lumber community wealthy from the work of its woodcutters and trappers, [location:9423110|Thundertree] now stands as a desolate, choked ghost town on the outskirts of the Neverwinter Wood. The village was utterly devastated decades ago by the catastrophic eruption of Mount Hotenow, which blanketed the area in ash and unleashed a horrific plague of ash zombies that drove away or killed any remaining survivors. Today, nature has aggressively reclaimed the ruins; ramshackle stone cottages are half-swallowed by dense, overgrown thickets, and a strange, mutating magic permeates the region, twisting the local vegetation into hostile, predatory plant monsters like twig blights. A heavy silence hangs over the crumbling village, broken only by the skittering of giant spiders and the ominous shadow of the young green dragon, Venomfang, who has claimed the town’s highest stone tower as his personal lair.

previous_entry: [location:9419635|Phandalin] is a rough-and-tumble frontier town nestled in the foothills of the Sword Mountains, built directly upon the stone ruins of a much larger human settlement that was destroyed centuries ago. Reclaimed by recent influxes of farmers, prospectors, and traders from nearby cities like Neverwinter, the bustling village features simple log buildings and dirt roads contrasted against crumbling, moss-covered archways. A single, muddy main street cuts through the heart of town, rising uphill toward the looming, dilapidated remains of Tresendar Manor. Because it lacks a formal city guard or military presence, [location:9419635|Phandalin] has a lawless, untamed atmosphere—making it a perfect haven for opportunistic mining exchanges, eccentric locals, and the ruthless criminal syndicates that seek to squeeze the town for everything it's worth.

Qualities that both share include striking good looks, a love of drink, and a flair for diplomacy. What Renaer lacks is his father's belligerence, ill temper, and bad judgment.  

Renaer lives off a sizable inheritance left to him by his mother, Alethea Brandath. Approaching middle age, he has given up adventuring and "settled down" somewhat. As a member of the [organisation:9419383], he spends a lot of time defending Waterdavians against those who, like his father, would deprive them of their coin and rights.  

He owns Brandarthall, a fourstory residence in the [location:9431883]. Renaer spends as little time there as possible, however, since it's constantly under surveillance by spies loyal to his father. His friends have an open invitation to use the house as they please, while Renaer spends most of his free time in taverns and festhalls.  

Some believe that Renaer's estrangement from his father is nothing but an act. and that anyone who bears the Neverember name is an enemy of [location:9418490]. Renaer just shakes his head at such accusations and gets on with his life. He has many powerful friends to watch his back.

previous_entry:
In terms of both geography and power, Castle Ward is the city's center. Most, if not all, of the city's administrative buildings are within the ward boundaries, from the lofty spires of Piergeiron's Palace to the low-slung crenelations of the guard smithy. While money and social standing are the prevalent benchmarks of might in the City of Splendors, [location:9418490]'s true power and what keeps it running are the Lords and Magisters here. If you like the taste of power and authority mixed with the usual commerce of the city, Castle Ward is the place to go.

The city guard maintains a strong presence in Castle Ward due to the concentration of city officials and areas of importance in need of heavier security. Even so, the watch maintains much of the order, especially around the Market, the Palace, and the Castle Ward docks. Like the guard, the watch makes a show of force in Castle Ward, traveling in larger patrols of six and brandishing short swords in addition to their normal rods and clubs.

The ward boundaries are the southern side of Julthoon Street over to Shield Street and down to Trader's Way on the north, meeting up with the High Road and Snail Street for the eastern perimeter. Lackpurse Lane, Belnimbra's Street, Gut Alley, and Shesstra's Street combine in an uneven boundary to the south, whereas the mountain and the coastline form the western edges of the ward. proposed_entry: In terms of both geography and power, Castle Ward is the city's center. Most, if not all, of the city's administrative buildings are within the ward boundaries, from the lofty spires of Piergeiron's Palace to the low-slung crenelations of the guard smithy. While money and social standing are the prevalent benchmarks of might in the City of Splendors, Waterdeep's true power and what keeps it running are the Lords and Magisters here. If you like the taste of power and authority mixed with the usual commerce of the city, Castle Ward is the place to go.  The city guard maintains a strong presence in Castle Ward due to the concentration of city officials and areas of importance in need of heavier security. Even so, the watch maintains much of the order, especially around the Market, the Palace, and the Castle Ward docks. Like the guard, the watch makes a show of force in Castle Ward, traveling in larger patrols of six and brandishing short swords in addition to their normal rods and clubs. previous_entry:
With no distinct look to separate it from surrounding wards, Trades Ward is somewhat lost in terms of neighborhood identity. On the other hand, though it lacks in neighborhood "feel," its sense of community in commerce occupies nearly every building and person within the entire ward. Many of [location:9418490]'s middle class and merchant class live and work here.

The busiest of wards due to all the constant commercial work within its boundaries, Trades Ward is active day and night, requiring excessive streetlights (many merchants say that Trades Ward at night is beautiful, "when her streets are filled with the stars of Waukeen"). The Guild of Chandlers and Lamplighters keeps a triple shift here at all times of the night, its streets filled with the bobbing lanterns of young lamplighters; the only more frequent sights in Trades Ward at night are the large and frequent watch patrols. While cursing, shoving, and minor street tussles are typical behavior within this business district, the worst criminal offenses are theft, vandalism, and destruction of private property - the watch patrols are more often needed to protect thieves from angry merchants than to stop robberies!

The ward boundaries are defined by the city walls and the City of the Dead on the east, and Andamaar's Street to the High Road on the north. The High Road and Snail Street border it on the west until Shesstra's Street cuts east to the Way of the Dragon where it links with the northern boundary of Southern Ward. Due to its central nature and rambling boundaries, it is hard to traverse the city without passing through this ward at some point.

Renaer lives off a sizable inheritance left to him by his mother, Alethea Brandath. Approaching middle age, he has given up adventuring and "settled down" somewhat. As a member of the [organisation:9419383], he spends a lot of time defending Waterdavians against those who, like his father, would deprive them of their coin and rights.  

He owns Brandarthall, a fourstory residence in the [location:9431883]. Renaer spends as little time there as possible, however, since it's constantly under surveillance by spies loyal to his father. His friends have an open invitation to use the house as they please, while Renaer spends most of his free time in taverns and festhalls.  

Some believe that Renaer's estrangement from his father is nothing but an act. and that anyone who bears the Neverember name is an enemy of [location:9418490]. Renaer just shakes his head at such accusations and gets on with his life. He has many powerful friends to watch his back.

Despite its reputation for safety, the ward's alleys and warehouses can become the site of violent turf wars between criminal organizations like the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] and the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild].

Southern Ward, known as South Ward to all natives, is the first ward seen by most visitors who enter the city through the South Gate or the River Gate with the caravans. As much of its business caters to the caravan trade, it is sometimes called Caravan City with its plentiful forges, smithies, stables, warehouses, and sheds (with coaches and carts for hire). Many common and poorer folk dwell in South Ward, though the caravan trade allows for some local merchants to attain near-noble status (at least in monetary terms). It is often dusty and grimy from the traffic from overland trade, but this area and its people are mostly friendly and industrious, catering to every need of visitors and merchant-traders. Tourists and visitors rarely idle around to look into wagons and warehouses (unless it is their business to do so), but the presence of guards (both privately hired and those in the watch) is obvious and lends much to the feeling of security about the trade goods and the businesses herein.

One of the smallest wards in the city, South Ward had probably the least to do with the internal politics (both social and monetary) of the city beyond the overland trades. South Ward is, for the most part, the ordinary or commoners' side of [location:9418490]. The main streets within the ward are the Way of the Dragon and the High Road. The Way of the Dragon forms the southern and western boundaries of South Ward, and the Troll Wall is the eastern boundary. The northern boundary consists of a mix of streets and alleys: Telshambra's Street, a little bit of the High Road, Sahtyra's Lane, Caravan Court (all of which is deemed to be in South Ward), and Belzer's Walk.

Recently, Renaer was kidnapped by [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] thugs who were searching for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] in connection to alleged embezzlement by his father. He was discovered by a group of adventurers hiding in a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward]. During the rescue, it was revealed that his friend [character:9431741|Floon] was also abducted by the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] in the confusion.

previous_entry: Xanathar is a powerful beholder who rules the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] from the depths beneath [location:9418490|Waterdeep], serving as both its absolute master and its most volatile weakness. Obsessed with control, treasure, and above all else paranoia, Xanathar maintains a sprawling criminal empire that extends through every level of the city’s underworld—smuggling, extortion, assassination, and intelligence gathering all ultimately feeding back to its central, ever-watching eye. As a beholder, it possesses vast innate magical power and a terrifying array of eye rays, but its greatest threat to its own organization is its obsessive suspicion, as it constantly believes (often correctly) that its own lieutenants are plotting betrayal. This paranoia leads to frequent purges within the guild, making Xanathar both an immensely stable source of power and an unpredictable, dangerous master. The guild is known to engage in violent skirmishes with rival factions, such as the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim], for control of the city's underworld. Recently, the guild has been actively hunting for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], an artifact that was previously in their possession before being stolen. The guild's reach is further evidenced by its use of high-level assets, such as the Mind Flayer [character:9432251|Nihiloor], who was recently deployed to orchestrate the kidnapping and torture of [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar].

previous_entry:
As the wealthiest ward of the city, Sea Ward is the seat of power for the established noble houses. Nearly empty during the winter due to the fierce sea storms, many of the nobles, well-to-do merchants, and social climbers call this home in the summer. Walking along the Street of the Singing Dolphin, the major avenue for the ward, one can expect to spot many of the grandest homes in [location:9418490], from the spires and gables of noble villas to the craggy and mysterious turrets of the wizards' towers. Sea Ward also contains many of the city's temples and Heroes' Garden, the only public garden outside the City of the Dead. Truly important (and self-important) people come to this ward to build their opulent homes while more modest folk or those more entrenched in the everyday politics and power of the city often choose to live in [location:9431892].

As with [location:9431893], watch patrols are quite frequent as one of the benefits of position. They are always polite and generally lightly armed, as most of the miscreants they find in this ward are well-dressed, drunken nobles who need only to be steered to the next party. The Watch deals swiftly with any other disruptions, their tolerance for any vandalism, violence, or theft being quite low.

The boundaries for this district are Julthoon Street and Shield Street, with a small eastern arm extending to the High road along Vondil Street.

[character:9425235|Alyzira Galanodel] is a half-elf bard who carries herself with a slender yet athletic build. Strikingly charming and inherently charismatic, she naturally steps forward as the eloquent, persuasive "face" of her adventuring party during high-stakes negotiations and social maneuvers. Her true passion lies in performance—where her sharp wits and musical talents shine beautifully in private or casual settings. However, [character:9425235|Alyzira] harbors a hilarious and deeply ironic curse: the moment a formal audience gathers to watch her perform, her standard bardic grace utterly vanishes, transforming her otherwise masterful art into a brilliantly comedic disaster.

Recently, [character:9425235|Alyzira] assisted in an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], where she successfully picked a front door lock to grant her party entry. During a confrontation with the City Watch, she utilized her persuasive skills to fast-talk Captain [character:9432045|Hyustus Staget], successfully explaining the party's presence and helping to avoid legal repercussions for the group.

During a recent excursion into the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, [character:9425235|Alyzira] was briefly stunned and mentally incapacitated when a [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] leaped onto her during a skirmish with the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Following the battle, she gathered the remaining coin and valuables from the site. She also played a pivotal role in securing the party's new base, using her magic to probe and calm a resident poltergeist named Leif within [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], successfully negotiating the spirit's demands for a thorough cleaning of the property.

[character:9425236|Eoula] is a diminutive female halfling ranger of mature years, possessing an exceptionally light and delicate frame. Deeply intellectual, she harbors a profound love for books and reading, though this quiet studiousness leaves her horribly awkward and out of her element in social situations. In combat, she primarily trusts her shortbow, but she also delights in unleashing sticky webs from her prized spider staff—a choice of weaponry wrapped in deep irony, given her intense dislike of actual spiders. Above all, [character:9425236|Eoula] possesses a fiercely compassionate heart for animals, driven by a protective nature that simply cannot bear to see creatures of the wild come to any harm.

During a recent investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], [character:9425236|Eoula] demonstrated her tactical utility by using her [ability:9442180|Web] spell to neutralize a group of Kenku ambushers. During the same investigation, she discovered [character:9431743|Renaer Neverember] hiding in a small room, where he provided crucial information regarding the disappearance of [character:9431741|Floon] and the search for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr].

More recently, [character:9425236|Eoula] navigated the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers and successfully rescued [character:9431741|Floon] from the clutches of the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. During the confrontation, she attempted to snatch a stone eye necklace from the Mind Flayer [character:9432251|Nihiloor] but was tossed aside as he escaped through a magical portal. Following the rescue, [character:9425236|Eoula] initially expressed a desire for signed copies of [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm]’s books as payment for the rescue, though she ultimately agreed to the group's acquisition of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor].

The Dock Ward of [location:9418490] is the rough, bustling heart of the city’s working waterfront, where sailors, dockworkers, fishmongers, merchants, and smugglers all collide in a constant churn of commerce and chaos. It is one of the most densely packed and colorful districts in Waterdeep, filled with creaking warehouses, leaning tenements, noisy taverns, and narrow streets that smell of saltwater, tar, and spilled ale. Ships from across the [location:9418394] and beyond crowd its piers, bringing goods, rumors, and trouble in equal measure. While officially under the protection of the City Watch, the Dock Ward is notoriously difficult to police completely, and many of its darker dealings are quietly influenced by criminal factions and dockside power brokers. Despite its grime and danger, it is also a place of opportunity, where fortunes can be made quickly—and lost even faster.

"If you want to understand Waterdeep, don’t start in the palace halls or noble villas—start at the docks. Everything that enters the city passes through here, and so does everything the city would rather forget."

[character:9425238|Tyde Undertow] is a striking, fey-touched or tiefling-like druid whose appearance beautifully bridges the gap between the wild earth and the deep ocean with vibrant blue skin transitioning into soft pink and silver tones across their limbs. Though her favorite wildshape forms for a fierce battle are a predatory wolf or a snapping crocodile, [character:9425238|Tyde]'s greatest challenge isn't a formidable enemy, but a simple map. Possessing absolutely zero sense of direction, she is blissfully incapable of getting from point A to point B without a guide, turning every simple journey into an accidental detour through the wilderness.

Tyde was found lost in the sewers of [location:9418490|Waterdeep] while searching for nature. After being spotted by [organisation:9419162|the party], she joined their ranks. [location:9418490] has long been a bastion of justice and the rule of law in the North (or at least has aspired to be such), thanks in large part to the followers of the Triad who have long played an illustrious role in the governance of the City of Splendors. A busy place popular with many Magistrates, Watch, and bureaucrats, the Halls of Justice are a towering edifice divided among several holy orders: the largest two being the Holy Justices of the Church of Tyr and the interfaith [organisation:9419404]. The front of this bookstore is adorned with a charming sign of a gold dragon curled around a treasure hoard of books and scrolls. Inside, the shop is decorated with beautiful hardwood, and the earthy scent of old books permeates the air. The library fills two floors of this three-story building, and it somehow seems to contain more shelves than the building should be able to hold.

The shop is managed by a short dragonborn of gold dragon ancestry named [character:9442098] the Page-Turner, who lives on the third floor. [character:9442098], a member of the Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors, is a mage.

The shop contains books of all sorts. In addition, [character:9442098] has a small collection of spellbooks and charges wizards to copy spells from them. He can scribe any of these spells as a scroll, and allows those with guild approval to copy spells from their source spellbooks for half this price.

[character:9423629|Orlum] is a gray-green tortle paladin who cuts an imposing figure with his tall stature and immense, heavy build. Bound by holy oaths, he possesses a remarkably straightforward and earnest mind, though his social interactions are often marked by a charming quirk: he takes whatever people say entirely literally, often missing figures of speech or sarcasm completely. Despite his formidable presence and martial devotion, [character:9423629|Orlum] harbors a gentle appreciation for sweet simple comforts. This is best exemplified by his absolute favorite possession—a magical pumpkin cupcake that miraculously replenishes itself, ensuring he is never without his preferred treat.

During a recent skirmish in a Candle Lane alleyway, Orlum demonstrated his martial prowess by decisively cleaving one of the attackers in half. During a recent investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse], Orlum successfully looted approximately 140 lbs of silver, a weight that left him heavily encumbered during the party's subsequent descent into the sewers. More recently, while navigating the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, Orlum faced a Mind Flayer named [character:9432251|Nihiloor]. Orlum attempted to block the Mind Flayer's path but was briefly dominated by its overwhelming psychic powers. However, he managed to break free of the mind control and decisively killed a half-orc named [character:9432250|Grum'shar] in a single hit.

Recently, Orlum traveled to the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] to attend an opera, where he slipped away with [character:9425238|Tyde] and [character:9419631|Raucous] to meet [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless." Following this meeting, the party has begun investigating leads regarding the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] and the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Most recently, Orlum assisted in a quest to stop living scarecrows terrorizing the farmlands of Undercliff Way. During the investigation, he cast Zone of Truth over a group of local farmers to help uncover the truth behind the terror, eventually leading to the capture of a witch named Donya who had animated the creatures.

In its modern state, it has been reclaimed and restored by adventurers, transforming it into a functional base of operations, tavern, and gathering place for allies, contacts, and faction agents. The Field Ward of [location:9418490] is an unofficial ward of the city, located between the inner and outer walls on the north side of town. It is in fact the city's slums — possessing the poorest living conditions within the city, is rife with crime, and serves as a home to the most destitute Waterdhavian citizens.

The ward has muddy, unpaved streets and no sanitation services or working sewer system. It is especially crowded, noisy and foul-smelling — stinking of slaughter-houses, tanneries, and waste. These guild businesses whose industries are rather offensive to the nose and ears are all relegated to the Field Ward, outside the city proper. Many poor elves, half-breeds, servants, homeless squatters, and other disregarded Waterdhavians, such as those with obvious deformities, call this district their home.  

The City Watch does not patrol here, but the City Guard watches over the road between the inner and outer gates to protect those passing through.

[character:9425235|Alyzira Galanodel] is a half-elf bard who carries herself with a slender yet athletic build. Strikingly charming and inherently charismatic, she naturally steps forward as the eloquent, persuasive "face" of her adventuring party during high-stakes negotiations and social maneuvers. Her true passion lies in performance—where her sharp wits and musical talents shine beautifully in private or casual settings. However, [character:9425235|Alyzira] harbors a hilarious and deeply ironic curse: the moment a formal audience gathers to watch her perform, her standard bardic grace utterly vanishes, transforming her otherwise masterful art into a brilliantly comedic disaster.

Recently, [character:9425235|Alyzira] assisted in an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], where she successfully picked a front door lock to grant her party entry. During a confrontation with the City Watch, she utilized her persuasive skills to fast-talk Captain [character:9432045|Hyustus Staget], successfully explaining the party's presence and helping to avoid legal repercussions for the group. During a recent excursion into the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, [character:9425235|Alyzira] was briefly stunned and mentally incapacitated when a [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] leaped onto her during a skirmish with the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Following the battle, she gathered the remaining coin and valuables from the site. She also played a pivotal role in securing the party's new base, using her magic to probe and calm a resident poltergeist named Leif within [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], successfully negotiating the spirit's demands for a thorough cleaning of the property.

Alyzira has recently expanded her influence and connections within the city. She successfully distracted a theater attendant at the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] to facilitate a clandestine meeting with [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless" of the [organisation:9419383|Harpers]. Furthermore, she was formally welcomed into the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave] by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon] at the [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], where she received a [item:9435948|charm of restoration].

During a recent quest for the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], Alyzira helped investigate reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the [location:9437517] farmlands. She used her magic to detect the thoughts of one of the creatures, identifying its eerie mental chant, and destroyed it with a Fireball. She also played a key role in the investigation of the local farmers, eventually using her charm magic to compel a local woman named Donya to confess to animating the creatures. For her efforts in saving the farmlands, Alyzira earned +1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave].

In a recent skirmish in the [location:9438959|Field Ward], Alyzira was involved in a brawl between rival thugs. While attempting to use non-lethal means to break up the fight, she accidentally dealt fatal blows, killing two of the thugs.

[character:9425236|Eoula] is a diminutive female halfling ranger of mature years, possessing an exceptionally light and delicate frame. Deeply intellectual, she harbors a profound love for books and reading, though this quiet studiousness leaves her horribly awkward and out of her element in social situations. In combat, she primarily trusts her shortbow, but she also delights in unleashing sticky webs from her prized spider staff—a choice of weaponry wrapped in deep irony, given her intense dislike of actual spiders. Above all, [character:9425236|Eoula] possesses a fiercely compassionate heart for animals, driven by a protective nature that simply cannot bear to see creatures of the wild come to any harm.

During a recent investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], [character:9425236|Eoula] demonstrated her tactical utility by using her [ability:9442180|Web] spell to neutralize a group of Kenku ambushers. During the same investigation, she discovered [character:9431743|Renaer Neverember] hiding in a small room, where he provided crucial information regarding the disappearance of [character:9431741|Floon] and the search for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr].

More recently, [character:9425236|Eoula] navigated the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers and successfully rescued [character:9431741|Floon] from the clutches of the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. During the confrontation, she attempted to snatch a stone eye necklace from the Mind Flayer [character:9432251|Nihiloor] but was tossed aside as he escaped through a magical portal. Following the rescue, [character:9425236|Eoula] initially expressed a desire for signed copies of [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm]’s books as payment for the rescue, though she ultimately agreed to the group's acquisition of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor].

Eoula recently traveled to the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] for an opera, where the party received a mission from the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] to locate a talking draft horse. She subsequently visited the [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa] in the [location:9435916|South Ward], where she was formally welcomed as a member of the local Enclave by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon]. As part of this membership, she was bestowed with a [item:9435948|charm of restoration].

While investigating reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the [location:9437517|Undercliff Way], [character:9425236|Eoula] utilized her tracking skills to follow stick-like footprints heading west. She also consulted her magical diary to uncover a local secret regarding the motives of the villagers involved. Following the successful neutralization of the scarecrows and the capture of the witch Donya, [character:9425236|Eoula] earned renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave].

Eoula recently visited the [location:9438977] to purchase a curious volume titled The [item:9438978] for 25 gold pieces. She also participated in the group's efforts to fund the renovations and guild fees for [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], which has now been successfully funded.

previous_entry: Trollskull Manor is a historic, formerly abandoned townhouse and tavern located in [location:9419015] within [location:9418490]’s [location:9431893|North Ward]. Once a lively neighborhood tavern known as the “Trollskull,” the building fell into disrepair after a tragic fire and years of neglect, becoming a decaying but character-filled ruin with a distinctive troll skull mounted on its roof. In its modern state, it has been reclaimed and restored by adventurers, transforming it into a functional base of operations, tavern, and gathering place for allies, contacts, and faction agents. Its rooms include common halls, private chambers, and upper floors that often serve as living quarters, meeting spaces, and storage for quests and loot. The property was recently acquired by [organisation:9419162|the party] from [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm] following the rescue of [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar]. While the manor is a majestic four-story property, it remains a significant renovation project. The rumors of a haunting were proven true upon the party's arrival; the manor is inhabited by a poltergeist who identifies as “Leif” (Lif). This ghost is a self-proclaimed neat-freak who has made it clear that he demands the messy, run-down inn be thoroughly cleaned. previous_entry: [character:9425235|Alyzira Galanodel] is a half-elf bard who carries herself with a slender yet athletic build. Strikingly charming and inherently charismatic, she naturally steps forward as the eloquent, persuasive "face" of her adventuring party during high-stakes negotiations and social maneuvers. Her true passion lies in performance—where her sharp wits and musical talents shine beautifully in private or casual settings. However, [character:9425235|Alyzira] harbors a hilarious and deeply ironic curse: the moment a formal audience gathers to watch her perform, her standard bardic grace utterly vanishes, transforming her otherwise masterful art into a brilliantly comedic disaster. Recently, [character:9425235|Alyzira] assisted in an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], where she successfully picked a front door lock to grant her party entry. During a confrontation with the City Watch, she utilized her persuasive skills to fast-talk Captain [character:9432045|Hyustus Staget], successfully explaining the party's presence and helping to avoid legal repercussions for the group. During a recent excursion into the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, [character:9425235|Alyzira] was briefly stunned and mentally incapacitated when a [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] leaped onto her during a skirmish with the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Following the battle, she gathered the remaining coin and valuables from the site. She also played a pivotal role in securing the party's new base, using her magic to probe and calm a resident poltergeist named Leif within [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], successfully negotiating the spirit's demands for a thorough cleaning of the property. Alyzira has recently expanded her influence and connections within the city. She successfully distracted a theater attendant at the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] to facilitate a clandestine meeting with [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless" of the [organisation:9419383|Harpers]. Furthermore, she was formally welcomed into the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave] by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon] at the [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], where she received a [item:9435948|charm of restoration]. During a recent quest for the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], Alyzira helped investigate reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the [location:9437517] farmlands. She used her magic to detect the thoughts of one of the creatures, identifying its eerie mental chant, and destroyed it with a Fireball. She also played a key role in the investigation of the local farmers, eventually using her charm magic to compel a local woman named Donya to confess to animating the creatures. For her efforts in saving the farmlands, Alyzira earned +1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave]. In a recent skirmish in the [location:9438959|Field Ward], Alyzira was involved in a brawl between rival thugs. While attempting to use non-lethal means to break up the fight, she accidentally dealt fatal blows, killing two of the thugs. Most recently, while exploring the neighborhood around [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], Alyzira engaged in community building by distributing invitations for a free drink to local shopkeepers. After patrolling the grounds and surviving an ambush of skeletons, she helped breach a shrine to confront Priest [character:9442159], who was being controlled by a glowing geometric tablet. Following the successful capture of the priest, Alyzira earned an additional +1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave].

Ornate iron gates open onto manicured grounds dotted with flowering trees and winding paths that lead to a grand two-story mansion of polished brick and dark timber. Inside, soaring ceilings, crystal chandeliers, rich mahogany furnishings, family portraits, and lavish tapestries speak to generations of prosperity, while the atmosphere carries an undercurrent of tension—as though every polished surface conceals a hidden agenda. Though outwardly the home of a respected noble family, the villa feels less like a residence and more like a fortress of intrigue, where loyal servants, hired guards, and whispered schemes lurk behind every closed door.

[organisation:9419162] discovered that he was spying on them throughout the events of Dragon Heist because he wanted the [item:9432044] for himself. previous_entry:
Renaer is the estranged son of [character:9457192|Dagult Neverember], the former Open Lord of Waterdeep and the current Lord of Neverwinter. Father and son detest one another. Renaer is least happy when he finds himself forced to deal with some mess his father left behind.

Qualities that both share include striking good looks, a love of drink, and a flair for diplomacy. What Renaer lacks is his father's belligerence, ill temper, and bad judgment.

Renaer lives off a sizable inheritance left to him by his mother, Alethea Brandath. Approaching middle age, he has given up adventuring and "settled down" somewhat. As a member of the [organisation:9419383], he spends a lot of time defending Waterdavians against those who, like his father, would deprive them of their coin and rights.

He owns [location:9443317|Brandarthall], a four-story residence in the [location:9431883]. Renaer spends as little time there as possible, however, since it's constantly under surveillance by spies loyal to his father. His friends have an open invitation to use the house as they please, while Renaer spends most of his free time in taverns and festhalls.

Some believe that Renaer's estrangement from his father is nothing but an act, and that anyone who bears the Neverember name is an enemy of [location:9418490]. Renaer just shakes his head at such accusations and gets on with his life. He has many powerful friends to watch his back.

Recently, Renaer was kidnapped by [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] thugs who were searching for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] in connection to alleged embezzlement by his father. He was discovered by a group of adventurers hiding in a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward]. During the rescue, it was revealed that his friend [character:9431741|Floon] was also abducted by the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] in the confusion.

Renaer has recently acted as a patron for the party, providing a recommendation that allowed [character:9435899|Mirt] to officially recruit [character:9419631|Raucous] into the [organisation:9419383].

proposed_entry:
Zardoz Zord is a flamboyant, jovial, kind, and gracious man. Unconcerned with city politics, his only aim is to bring joy and wonder to the hearts of people everywhere. He is the owner of the Sea Maidens Faire, a traveling carnival that has brought three galleons—the Heartbreaker, the Hellraiser, and his flashy flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher]—to [location:9418490|Waterdeep]. 

When not cavorting around the city promoting the debut of the Sea Maiden's Faire, he spends his time on his personal ship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher], anchored in the harbor, rehearsing with his all-human crew, indulging in his weakness for delectable foods and libations, or seducing any man or woman that stirs his loins. He is known to visit the distant island of Lantan once a year, from which he recently purchased four nimblewrights to serve as performing automatons aboard his vessels.
change_summary: Updated the synopsis to include details about his ownership of the Sea Maidens Faire carnival, his specific ships (including the flagship Eyecatcher), and his recent purchase of nimblewrights from Lantan. Added a new relationship regarding his affair with Lady Gralhund.

previous_entry: [character:9423629|Orlum] is a gray-green tortle paladin who cuts an imposing figure with his tall stature and immense, heavy build. Bound by holy oaths, he possesses a remarkably straightforward and earnest mind, though his social interactions are often marked by a charming quirk: he takes whatever people say entirely literally, often missing figures of speech or sarcasm completely. Despite his formidable presence and martial devotion, [character:9423629|Orlum] harbors a gentle appreciation for sweet simple comforts. This is best exemplified by his absolute favorite possession—a magical pumpkin cupcake that miraculously replenishes itself, ensuring he is never without his preferred treat. During a recent skirmish in a Candle Lane alleyway, Orlum demonstrated his martial prowess by decisively cleaving one of the attackers in half. During a recent investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse], Orlum successfully looted approximately 140 lbs of silver, a weight that left him heavily encumbered during the party's subsequent descent into the sewers. More recently, while navigating the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, Orlum faced a Mind Flayer named [character:9432251|Nihiloor]. Orlum attempted to block the Mind Flayer's path but was briefly dominated by its overwhelming psychic powers. However, he managed to break free of the mind control and decisively killed a half-orc named [character:9432250|Grum'shar] in a single hit. Recently, Orlum traveled to the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] to attend an opera, where he slipped away with [character:9425238|Tyde] and [character:9419631|Raucous] to meet [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless." Following this meeting, the party has begun investigating leads regarding the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] and the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Most recently, Orlum assisted in a quest to stop living scarecrows terrorizing the farmlands of Undercliff Way. During the investigation, he cast Zone of Truth over a group of local farmers to help uncover the truth behind the terror, eventually leading to the capture of a witch named Donya who had animated the creatures. Following a request from the [organisation:9419404], Orlum intervened in a gang war in the [location:9438959] to stop turf wars between rival thugs. For his efforts in keeping the peace, he was formally initiated into the [organisation:9419404] at the grand [location:9438976] in the [location:9431892], earning 1 Renown with the Order. More recently, Orlum and his companions responded to an urgent request from the [organisation:9419386] regarding a necromantic threat in the [location:9438979]. While patrolling the graveyard, the party was ambushed by skeletons. During a confrontation at the [location:9442141], Orlum rushed through flames to smash a glowing geometric artifact tablet, which successfully freed Priest [character:9442159] from a dark thrall. Following the capture of the priest, Orlum and his allies earned 1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386].

previous_entry: [character:9425235|Alyzira Galanodel] is a half-elf bard who carries herself with a slender yet athletic build. Strikingly charming and inherently charismatic, she naturally steps forward as the eloquent, persuasive "face" of her adventuring party during high-stakes negotiations and social maneuvers. Her true passion lies in performance—where her sharp wits and musical talents shine beautifully in private or casual settings. However, [character:9425235|Alyzira] harbors a hilarious and deeply ironic curse: the moment a formal audience gathers to watch her perform, her standard bardic grace utterly vanishes, transforming her otherwise masterful art into a brilliantly comedic disaster. Recently, [character:9425235|Alyzira] assisted in an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], where she successfully picked a front door lock to grant her party entry. During a confrontation with the City Watch, she utilized her persuasive skills to fast-talk Captain [character:9432045|Hyustus Staget], successfully explaining [organisation:9419162|the party]'s presence and helping to avoid legal repercussions for the group. During a recent excursion into the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, [character:9425235|Alyzira] was briefly stunned and mentally incapacitated when an [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] leaped onto her during a skirmish with the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Following the battle, she gathered the remaining coin and valuables from the site. She also played a pivotal role in securing [organisation:9419162|the party]'s new base, using her magic to probe and calm a resident poltergeist named Leif within [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], successfully negotiating the spirit's demands for a thorough cleaning of the property. [character:9425235|Alyzira] has recently expanded her influence and connections within the city. She successfully distracted a theater attendant at the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] to facilitate a clandestine meeting with [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless" of the [organisation:9419383|Harpers]. Furthermore, she was formally welcomed into the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave] by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon] at the [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], where she received a [item:9435948|charm of restoration]. During a recent quest for the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], [character:9425235|Alyzira] helped investigate reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the outlying farmlands. She used her magic to detect the thoughts of one of the creatures, identifying its eerie mental chant, and destroyed it with a Fireball . She also played a key role in the investigation of the local farmers, eventually using her charm magic to compel a local woman named Donya to confess to animating the creatures. For her efforts in saving the farmlands, [character:9425235|Alyzira] earned +1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave]. Following a violent explosion in the alleyway outside [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] that left eleven people dead, [character:9425235|Alyzira] assisted in investigating the scene. She successfully coaxed a frightened halfling boy into giving her a broken necklace containing magical fireball gems, which she analyzed with magic before surrendering it to the City Watch. To further the investigation, she bribed a cleric with 25 gold pieces to arrange a Speak with Dead ritual involving a deceased gnome at Mystra's shrine in the [location:9438979|City of the Dead] cemetery. Additionally, during an investigation at the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] [location:9442786|House of Inspired Hands], she promptly picked a locked attic door to reveal a mute nimblewright automaton, [character:9442788|Nim]. Following a chaotic battle at [location:9443309|Gralhund Villa], [character:9425235|Alyzira] used her magic to charm [character:9443308|Urstul Floxin], a prominent member of the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim], uncovering vital intelligence regarding the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], a hidden half-million gold piece vault, and the Gralhund family's involvement in the alleyway explosion. Though she tried to secure his future cooperation, her party members prematurely released the untrustworthy thug, who immediately fled. To further their investigation into a mysterious rival thief known as the "[character:9443961|Black Viper]," [character:9425235|Alyzira] paid a 30 gold piece bribe to the publisher of the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] Wazoo , uncovering a lead that the thief might be the disfigured secret twin sister of [character:9443963|Ammalia Cassalanter]. In an effort to track the missing nimblewright, [character:9425235|Alyzira] coordinated with her ally [character:9423618|Gladio] to arrange an aerial search via a griffon. When the tracker led [organisation:9419162|the party] to the Sea Maidens Faire carnival in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward], [character:9425235|Alyzira] utilized her social charms to strike up a conversation with the crew, securing an exclusive invitation to dine with the flamboyant carnival master, [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord], aboard his flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher]. Though she was mortified when her companion [character:9423629|Orlum] performed a radical flute solo during the luxury feast, the dinner allowed [organisation:9419162|the party] to inspect [character:9443973|Zord]’s legally owned nimblewrights and deduce that [character:9442788|Nim]'s rogue creation was still loose in the city. Most recently, [character:9425235|Alyzira] and her party met secretly with high-ranking [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] agent [character:9443960|Istrid Horn] at Ahghairon’s Statue in the [location:9438979|City of the Dead]. Recognizing the benefits of a wealthy and well-connected ally, [character:9425235|Alyzira] and her party agreed to harbor the fugitive loan shark, helping disguise her as a male dwarf named Jorn to safely lay low at [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] ahead of the tavern's grand opening. With construction on [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] complete, [character:9425235|Alyzira] helped neutralize a rogue nimblewright in the [location:9435900|Trades Ward], which resulted in her receiving functional stilts as a reward from [location:9442786|House of Inspired Hands]. Following this, she and her party assisted [organisation:9419383|the Harpers] by defeating a gazer that had taken over a bookstore at [location:9445758], rescuing the shopkeeper's cat in the process. After the battle, she celebrated the tavern's opening with an "acceptable" musical rendition of Darude's "Sandstorm."

previous_entry:
Southern Ward, known as South Ward to all natives, is the first ward seen by most visitors who enter the city through the South Gate or the River Gate with the caravans. As much of its business caters to the caravan trade, it is sometimes called Caravan City with its plentiful forges, smithies, stables, warehouses, and sheds (with coaches and carts for hire). Many common and poorer folk dwell in South Ward, though the caravan trade allows for some local merchants to attain near-noble status (at least in monetary terms). It is often dusty and grimy from the traffic from overland trade, but this area and its people are mostly friendly and industrious, catering to every need of visitors and merchant-traders. Tourists and visitors rarely idle around to look into wagons and warehouses (unless it is their business to do so), but the presence of guards (both privately hired and those in the watch) is obvious and lends much to the feeling of security about the trade goods and the businesses herein.

One of the smallest wards in the city, South Ward had probably the least to do with the internal politics (both social and monetary) of the city beyond the overland trades. South Ward is, for the most part, the ordinary or commoners' side of [location:9418490]. The main streets within the ward are the Way of the Dragon and the High Road. The Way of the Dragon forms the southern and western boundaries of South Ward, and the Troll Wall is the eastern boundary. The northern boundary consists of a mix of streets and alleys: Telshambra's Street, a little bit of the High Road, Sahtyra's Lane, Caravan Court (all of which is deemed to be in South Ward), and Belzer's Walk. The ward is also home to the [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], a noble estate and a safe haven for members of the local Emerald Enclave.

Ruled by the mysterious Lords of Waterdeep and publicly represented by the Open Lord, the city thrives on trade, magic, and politics, drawing in wealth and danger from across [location:9418260] through its vast harbor and strategic position on the [location:9418394]. Beneath its grand estates, bustling wards, and famed institutions lies a labyrinth of secrets: ancient ruins, hidden guild operations, and conspiracies that can shape the fate of nations. The city's various wards, such as the [location:9431892|Castle Ward], the shadow-filled [location:9418606|Dock Ward], and the parkland cemetery known as the [location:9438979|City of the Dead], serve as backdrops for intense factional violence between groups like the [character:9419465|Xanathar] Guild and the Zhentarim. Waterdeep is both a beacon of opportunity and a maze of intrigue, where fortunes are made quickly—such as the rumored half-million gold vault hidden somewhere within its streets—but only by those clever enough to survive its many layers.

previous_entry: Xanathar is a powerful beholder who rules the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] from the depths beneath [location:9418490|Waterdeep], serving as both its absolute master and its most volatile weakness. Obsessed with control, treasure, and above all else paranoia, Xanathar maintains a sprawling criminal empire that extends through every level of the city’s underworld—smuggling, extortion, assassination, and intelligence gathering all ultimately feeding back to its central, ever-watching eye. As a beholder, it possesses vast innate magical power and a terrifying array of eye rays, but its greatest threat to its own organization is its obsessive suspicion, as it constantly believes (often correctly) that its own lieutenants are plotting betrayal. This paranoia leads to frequent purges within the guild, making Xanathar both an immensely stable source of power and an unpredictable, dangerous master. The guild is known to engage in violent skirmishes with rival factions, such as the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim], for control of the city's underworld. Recently, the guild has been actively hunting for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], an artifact that was previously in their possession before being stolen. The guild's reach is further evidenced by its use of high-level assets, such as the Mind Flayer [character:9432251|Nihiloor], who was recently deployed to orchestrate the kidnapping and torture of [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar]. Recent intelligence suggests that a dwarf is currently stealing an artifact belonging to the disgraced former Open Lord [character:9457192|Dagult Neverember] directly from the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Furthermore, the guild's interests are being threatened by a sun elf named [character:9435949|Davil Starsong] and his bodyguard [character:9431701|Yagra Stonefist], who have been actively hiring spies to hunt down [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] hideouts.

[character:9425235|Alyzira Galanodel] is a half-elf bard who carries herself with a slender yet athletic build. Strikingly charming and inherently charismatic, she naturally steps forward as the eloquent, persuasive "face" of her adventuring party during high-stakes negotiations and social maneuvers. Her true passion lies in performance—where her sharp wits and musical talents shine beautifully in private or casual settings. However, [character:9425235|Alyzira] harbors a hilarious and deeply ironic curse: the moment a formal audience gathers to watch her perform, her standard bardic grace utterly vanishes, transforming her otherwise masterful art into a brilliantly comedic disaster.

Recently, [character:9425235|Alyzira] assisted in an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], where she successfully picked a front door lock to grant her party entry. During a confrontation with the City Watch, she utilized her persuasive skills to fast-talk Captain [character:9432045|Hyustus Staget], successfully explaining [organisation:9419162|the party]'s presence and helping to avoid legal repercussions for the group. During a recent excursion into the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers, [character:9425235|Alyzira] was briefly stunned and mentally incapacitated when an [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] leaped onto her during a skirmish with the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Following the battle, she gathered the remaining coin and valuables from the site. She also played a pivotal role in securing [organisation:9419162|the party]'s new base, using her magic to probe and calm a resident poltergeist named Leif within [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], successfully negotiating the spirit's demands for a thorough cleaning of the property.

[character:9425235|Alyzira] has recently expanded her influence and connections within the city. Additionally, during an investigation at the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] [location:9442786|House of Inspired Hands], she promptly picked a locked attic door to reveal a mute nimblewright automaton, [character:9442788|Nim]. previous_entry: [character:9425236|Eoula] is a diminutive female halfling ranger of mature years, possessing an exceptionally light and delicate frame. Deeply intellectual, she harbors a profound love for books and reading, though this quiet studiousness leaves her horribly awkward and out of her element in social situations. In combat, she primarily trusts her shortbow, but she also delights in unleashing sticky webs from her prized spider staff—a choice of weaponry wrapped in deep irony, given her intense dislike of actual spiders. Above all, [character:9425236|Eoula] possesses a fiercely compassionate heart for animals, driven by a protective nature that simply cannot bear to see creatures of the wild come to any harm. During a recent investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], [character:9425236|Eoula] demonstrated her tactical utility by using her [ability:9442180|Web] spell to neutralize a group of Kenku ambushers. During the same investigation, she discovered [character:9431743|Renaer Neverember] hiding in a small room, where he provided crucial information regarding the disappearance of [character:9431741|Floon] and the search for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr]. More recently, [character:9425236|Eoula] navigated the [location:9418490|Waterdeep] sewers and successfully rescued [character:9431741|Floon] from the clutches of the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. During the confrontation, she attempted to snatch a stone eye necklace from the Mind Flayer [character:9432251|Nihiloor] but was tossed aside as he escaped through a magical portal. Following the rescue, [character:9425236|Eoula] initially expressed a desire for signed copies of [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm]’s books as payment for the rescue, though she ultimately agreed to the group's acquisition of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor]. [character:9425236|Eoula] recently traveled to the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] for an opera, where [organisation:9419162|the party] received a mission from the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] to locate a talking draft horse. She subsequently visited the [location:9435917|Phaulkononmere Villa] in the [location:9435916|South Ward], where she was formally welcomed as a member of the local Enclave by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon]. As part of this membership, she was bestowed with a [item:9435948|charm of restoration]. While investigating reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the [location:9437517|Undercliff Way], [character:9425236|Eoula] utilized her tracking skills to follow stick-like footprints heading west. She also consulted her magical diary to uncover a local secret regarding the motives of the villagers involved. Following the successful neutralization of the scarecrows and the capture of the witch Donya, [character:9425236|Eoula] earned renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave]. [character:9425236|Eoula] recently visited the [location:9438977] to purchase a curious volume titled The [item:9438978] for 25 gold pieces. She also participated in the group's efforts to fund the renovations and guild fees for [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], which has now been successfully funded. During a neighborhood stroll through [location:9419015], she performed community outreach by handing out invitations for a free drink at [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] to local shopkeepers. Most recently, while patrolling the [location:9438979] (the local cemetery) on behalf of the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], she was ambushed by a group of skeletons. Following the skirmish, she used her [ability:9442180|Web] spell to restrain Priest [character:9442159], who was under the influence of a dark artifact. Her efforts, along with those of her companions, resulted in the successful capture of the priest and earned her additional renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave]. Following a devastating fireball explosion outside [location:9418605] that left eleven people dead, [character:9425236|Eoula] assisted in an investigation. Using her [item:9437393], she uncovered local trivia regarding Sergeant [character:9442769|Barnibus]'s toupee. [organisation:9419162|The party] subsequently traveled to the [location:9442786] (the Temple of Gond) to investigate a rogue nimblewright automaton. There, they met Lady [character:9442787], who offered a 500 gold piece reward for the destruction of the creature. After interacting with a mute nimblewright named [character:9442788], [organisation:9419162|the party] received a copper tracking device to aid in their hunt. Following this, while investigating the aftermath of the explosion, [character:9425236|Eoula] used her [item:9437393] to record information regarding Lady [character:9443310], uncovering that she has a secret lover, the drow [character:9443318]. [organisation:9419162|The party] then infiltrated [location:9443309], the estate of the Gralhund family, where they engaged in a skirmish with members of the [organisation:9419438] to defend house guards in the upstairs foyer. During this infiltration, [character:9425236|Eoula] uncovered scandalous gossip that [character:9443310|Lady Gralhund] is having an affair with the carnival master, [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord]. Additionally, while investigating a potential lead on the "[character:9443961|Black Viper]," she used her Gossiper's Diary to magically confirm that the thief is likely a disfigured woman. Following the Gralhund affair, [character:9425236|Eoula] and her companions met with [character:9443960|Istrid Horn], a high-ranking [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] agent. After receiving payment for the meeting, the group agreed to allow [character:9443960|Istrid Horn] to hide out at [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] under a disguise. With construction on [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] complete, [character:9425236|Eoula] has settled into the newly opened inn. Following the successful neutralization of a rogue nimblewright, she was rewarded with a pair of functional stilts. Recently, while consulting her [item:9437393], she uncovered further scandalous information regarding the affair between [character:9443310|Lady Gralhund] and [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord]. She also assisted the party in resolving a monster problem at a local bookstore, where they defeated a floating gazer and rescued a cat named Philippa. Following this, she has been preparing to address new faction requests from the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], the [organisation:9419404], and the [organisation:9419383|Harpers].

previous_entry: [character:9425238|Tyde Undertow] is a striking, fey-touched or tiefling-like druid whose appearance beautifully bridges the gap between the wild earth and the deep ocean with vibrant blue skin transitioning into soft pink and silver tones across their limbs. Though her favorite wildshape forms for a fierce battle are a predatory wolf or a snapping crocodile, [character:9425238|Tyde]'s greatest challenge isn't a formidable enemy, but a simple map. Possessing absolutely zero sense of direction, she is blissfully incapable of getting from point A to point B without a guide, turning every simple journey into an accidental detour through the wilderness. Tyde was found lost in the sewers of [location:9418490|Waterdeep] while searching for nature. After being spotted by [organisation:9419162|the party], she joined their ranks. She is now a member of [organisation:9419162|the party] and a resident of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor]. Recently, Tyde has begun expanding her ties with local factions. She was invited to join the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave] after a speaking cat approached her and [character:9425235|Alyzira]. She is particularly eager to work with the Enclave to locate her missing group of coastal druids. She was formally granted membership by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon] at [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], where she received a [item:9435948|charm of restoration] and a promise of assistance in finding her lost kin. Tyde recently assisted the party in investigating reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the [location:9437517] on Undercliff Way.  During an infiltration of [location:9443309], Tyde wildshaped into a wolf to help the party dispatch five [organisation:9419438] swordsmen. During this hunt, she used her tracking device to help corner a rogue nimblewright in the [location:9435900]. Following the battle, Tyde was rewarded with 100 gold pieces and a backpack parachute that negates fall damage.

 Tyde has continued her service to the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], recently engaging in combat against a pack of wererats from the [organisation:9453215] in Endshift Alley. Once a lively neighborhood tavern known as the “Trollskull,” the building fell into disrepair after a tragic fire and years of neglect, becoming a decaying but character-filled ruin with a distinctive troll skull mounted on its roof. In its modern state, it has been reclaimed and restored by adventurers, transforming it into a functional base of operations, tavern, and gathering place for allies, contacts, and faction agents.

While the manor remains inhabited by its resident poltergeist, “Leif” (Lif), the property has transitioned from a renovation project into a completed establishment. Recent activity includes the arrival of two suspicious halfling job applicants, [character:9445765] and [character:9445766], who visited the porch seeking employment.

The property was recently acquired by [organisation:9419162|the party] from [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm]. Despite its successful grand opening, the manor continues to serve as a hub for the party's various faction-related activities and investigations.

previous_entry:
The Field Ward of [location:9418490] is an unofficial ward of the city, located between the inner and outer walls on the north side of town. It is in fact the city's slums — possessing the poorest living conditions within the city, is rife with crime, and serves as a home to the most destitute Waterdhavian citizens.

The ward has muddy, unpaved streets and no sanitation services or working sewer system. It is especially crowded, noisy and foul-smelling — stinking of slaughter-houses, tanneries, and waste. These guild businesses whose industries are rather offensive to the nose and ears are all relegated to the Field Ward, outside the city proper. Many poor elves, half-breeds, servants, homeless squatters, and other disregarded Waterdhavians, such as those with obvious deformities, call this district their home.

The City Watch does not patrol here, but the City Guard watches over the road between the inner and outer gates to protect those passing through. The area is known for its rough-and-tumble atmosphere, frequently seeing turf wars and brawls between rival thugs.

A local [location:9418490|Waterdeep] butcher and friend of [character:9423618|Gladio], Raucous joined the party at the [location:9431699|Yawning Portal] amidst a tavern brawl and a monster outbreak from the central well. He has been acting as a guide for the group, leading them through the [location:9418606|Dock Ward] in their search for [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar]. During an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], Raucous accidentally triggered an alarm while exploring the upper level, which drew the attention of the City Watch. Raucous recently led the party in a successful rescue of [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar] from a [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] hideout in the sewers. During the skirmish, he looted a spellbook from the body of a half-orc named [character:9432250|Grum’shar]. Following the rescue, Raucous took the lead in escorting [character:9431741|Floon] back to the [location:9431699|Yawning Portal] to reunite with [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm]. The party subsequently acquired the deed to [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] in [location:9419015|Trollskull Alley] as payment for the rescue. Raucous was recently recruited into the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] by [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless" after attending an opera at the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater]. He was tasked with locating a talking draft horse mare named [character:9435910|Maxeene], who serves as a spy for the faction. After the horse was located, Raucous received a sealed envelope containing 100 gp and 1 Renown with the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] as a reward for his service.

Recently, Raucous has been involved in the party's efforts to fund the renovations of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] and prepare for the upcoming [event:9438944]. He participated in a mission to the [location:9438958] in the [location:9438959] to break up a gang war between rival thugs on behalf of the [organisation:9419404]. Most recently, he was part of the group that investigated a necromantic threat in the [location:9438979] at the request of the [organisation:9419386], resulting in the capture of Priest [character:9442159].

During a chaotic battle against the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] at [location:9443309|Gralhund Villa], Raucous untied the Zhentarim member [character:9443308|Urstul Floxin]. Following the completion of construction on [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], Raucous and his companions have been working through various faction-related tasks. previous_entry: The Dock Ward of [location:9418490] is the rough, bustling heart of the city’s working waterfront, where sailors, dockworkers, fishmongers, merchants, and smugglers all collide in a constant churn of commerce and chaos. It is one of the most densely packed and colorful districts in Waterdeep, filled with creaking warehouses, leaning tenements, noisy taverns, and narrow streets that smell of saltwater, tar, and spilled ale. Ships from across the [location:9418394] and beyond crowd its piers, bringing goods, rumors, and trouble in equal measure. Recent activity has seen a fleet of ships belonging to the Sea Maidens Faire carnival, owned by [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord], docking at the ward's piers. This includes the galleons Heartbreaker and Hellraiser, while their flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher], remains anchored in Deepwater Harbor. The area remains a focal point for tracking rogue automatons, as recent aerial searches have identified high concentrations of signal activity near these docked vessels. While officially under the protection of the City Watch, the Dock Ward is notoriously difficult to police completely, and many of its darker dealings are quietly influenced by criminal factions and dockside power brokers. Despite its grime and danger, it is also a place of opportunity, where fortunes can be made quickly—and lost even faster. "If you want to understand Waterdeep, don’t start in the palace halls or noble villas—start at the docks. Everything that enters the city passes through here, and so does everything the city would rather forget."

previous_entry: Laeral Silverhand is the current Open Lord of [location:9418490], a legendary archmage and former adventurer who now governs the City of Splendors with a rare blend of wisdom, restraint, and immense magical authority. As one of the famed Silverhand sisters and a Chosen of Mystra, she is deeply connected to the weave of magic itself, and her long life has given her both the patience to navigate Waterdeep’s complex politics and the resolve to act decisively when the city is threatened. Unlike more authoritarian rulers, Laeral tends to favor delegation through trusted institutions like the Lords of Waterdeep, the City Watch, and allied factions, intervening personally only when the stakes are truly dire. She is widely respected, if sometimes feared for what she could do if pushed too far, and she remains a stabilizing force in a city perpetually balanced between order and chaos.

previous_entry: Istrid is regarded as the Black Network's Master of Trade and Coin in [location:9418490]. The shield dwarf operates an illegal lending operation out of a heavily guarded warehouse in the [location:9418606], offering loans to those in need of coin. Her interest rates are comparable to those of her competitors (including noble families of bankers such as the Cassalanters and the Irlingstars), but the penalties for not paying back Istrid's loans are severe. Istrid worships Vergadain, the dwarven god of wealth and luck. She likes having others indebted to her, and she employs thugs and enforcers to collect on her loans. If those resources prove inadequate, Istrid can call on her old adventuring companions for assistance. Following the events at [location:9443309], Istrid reached out to [organisation:9419162|the party] to discuss the fallout of the Gralhund Villa massacre. She revealed that she had personally provided funding to the Gralhunds, who had been secretly bankrolling [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] operations. Fearing arrest by the City Watch due to her underground banking, she paid the party 10 platinum just to meet and offered an additional 40 platinum for them to let her hide at [location:9418605]. She is currently residing at [location:9418605] in disguise as a male dwarf named Jorn, promising to perform chores while she lays low.

previous_entry: With no distinct look to separate it from surrounding wards, Trades Ward is somewhat lost in terms of neighborhood identity. On the other hand, though it lacks in neighborhood "feel," its sense of community in commerce occupies nearly every building and person within the entire ward. Many of [location:9418490]'s middle class and merchant class live and work here. The busiest of wards due to all the constant commercial work within its boundaries, Trades Ward is active day and night, requiring excessive streetlights (many merchants say that Trades Ward at night is beautiful, "when her streets are filled with the stars of Waukeen"). The Guild of Chandlers and Lamplighters keeps a triple shift here at all times of the night, its streets filled with the bobbing lanterns of young lamplighters; the only more frequent sights in Trades Ward at night are the large and frequent watch patrols. While cursing, shoving, and minor street tussles are typical behavior within this business district, the worst criminal offenses are theft, vandalism, and destruction of private property - the watch patrols are more often needed to protect thieves from angry merchants than to stop robberies! The ward boundaries are defined by the city walls and the [location:9438979|City of the Dead] on the east, and Andamaar's Street to the High Road on the north. The High Road and Snail Street border it on the west until Shesstra's Street cuts east to the Way of the Dragon where it links with the northern boundary of Southern Ward. Due to its central nature and rambling boundaries, it is hard to traverse the city without passing through this ward at some point. The ward's commercial nature is further complicated by the presence of organized crime and the city's sprawling sewer system. While the streets are patrolled by the City Watch, the subterranean tunnels beneath the ward serve as a labyrinthine territory for various factions, including the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild].

Southern Ward, known as South Ward to all natives, is the first ward seen by most visitors who enter the city through the South Gate or the River Gate with the caravans. As much of its business caters to the caravan trade, it is sometimes called Caravan City with its plentiful forges, smithies, stables, warehouses, and sheds (with coaches and carts for hire). Many common and poorer folk dwell in South Ward, though the caravan trade allows for some local merchants to attain near-noble status (at least in monetary terms).

It is often dusty and grimy from the traffic from overland trade, but this area and its people are mostly friendly and industrious, catering to every need of visitors and merchant-traders. Tourists and visitors rarely idle around to look into wagons and warehouses (unless it is their business to do so), but the presence of guards (both privately hired and those in the watch) is obvious and lends much to the feeling of security about the trade goods and the businesses herein.

One of the smallest wards in the city, South Ward had probably the least to do with the internal politics (both social and monetary) of the city beyond the overland trades. South Ward is, for the most part, the ordinary or commoners' side of [location:9418490]. The main streets within the ward are the Way of the Dragon and the High Road. The Way of the Dragon forms the southern and western boundaries of South Ward, and the Troll Wall is the eastern boundary. The northern boundary consists of a mix of streets and alleys: Telshambra's Street, a little bit of the High Road, Sahtyra's Lane, Caravan Court (all of which is deemed to be in South Ward), and Belzer's Walk. The ward is also home to the [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], a noble estate and a safe haven for members of the local Emerald Enclave.

Currently, the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] maintains a secret cellar complex hidden underneath the [location:9435916|South Ward].
