proposed_entry:
[character:9425236|Eoula] is a diminutive female halfling ranger of mature years, possessing an exceptionally light and delicate frame. Deeply intellectual, she harbors a profound love for books and reading, though this quiet studiousness leaves her horribly awkward and out of her element in social situations. In combat, she primarily trusts her shortbow, but she also delights in unleashing sticky webs from her prized spider staff—a choice of weaponry wrapped in deep irony, given her intense dislike of actual spiders. Above all, [character:9425236|Eoula] possesses a fiercely compassionate heart for animals, driven by a protective nature that simply cannot bear to see creatures of the wild come to any harm.

During a recent mission following advice from Open Lord [character:9418614|Laerel Silverhand], [character:9425236|Eoula] and [organisation:9419162|the party] infiltrated the [location:9435916|South Ward] sewers to locate a hidden [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] outpost. During the infiltration, she was bolstered by [character:9425235|Alyzira], who cast *bear's endurance* on her to prepare for a clash with seven troglodytes and a gibbering mouther. After clearing the chambers, the group returned to [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] with what they believed was the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr]. However, it was soon discovered that the artifact was merely a cleverly painted rock.

Despite the setback with the counterfeit stone, the group successfully installed a mechanical beholder—a device recovered from the sewers—as a special attraction within [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor]. Following this discovery, [organisation:9419162|the party] is planning to visit the [location:9453223|Seven Masks Theater] in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward] to consult with "Laeral."
change_summary: Updated the synopsis to include the recent sewer infiltration, the combat against troglodytes and a gibbering mouther, the discovery that the 'Stone of Golorr' was a fake, and the installation of the mechanical beholder at Trollskull Manor.

previous_entry:
Home to the many wealthier middle class, lesser nobles, and well-to-do merchants, North Ward is a quiet haven from the hustle and bustle of [location:9418490]'s commercial endeavors. Dominated by residences, this ward tends toward insular, walled villas and distinctly individual stone and timber houses. While, on the surface, it seems tedious compared to the rest of the city, North Ward seethes with intrigues of far-reaching effects hidden just beneath the surface. There is little for visitors to do within this ward beyond gawk at the marvelous houses and towers unless they are already linked into the nobles' or guilds' politics. The city watch keeps this ward under tight control, suffering noise and disruption only from the local nobles and dandies while rousting noisy trespassers. Though lightly armed, the watch maintains a constant presence in North Ward, making it as safe as one can be in a city of this size. If ever a place "closes down upon the cobbles at dusk," North Ward fits the bill.

North Ward's western boundaries consist on the High Road with a western arm extending to Shield Street along Vondril Street and Trader's Way. Andamaar's Street marks the southern border, while the walls of the [location:9438979|City of the Dead] and the Trollwall close out the rest of the ward. Despite its reputation for safety, the ward's alleys and warehouses can become the site of violent turf wars between criminal organizations like the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] and the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild].

The ward is also home to [location:9431893|North Ward] property holdings, including [location:418605|Trollskull Manor], a majestic four-story property recently acquired by [organisation:9419162|the party] via a legal deed transfer overseen by Magistrate [character:9432255|Kylynne Silmerhelve].

[character:9425238|Tyde Undertow] is a striking, fey-touched or tiefling-like druid whose appearance beautifully bridges the gap between the wild earth and the deep ocean with vibrant blue skin transitioning into soft pink and silver tones across their limbs. Though her favorite wildshape forms for a fierce battle are a predatory wolf or a snapping crocodile, [character:9425238|Tyde]'s greatest challenge isn't a formidable enemy, but a simple map. Possessing absolutely zero sense of direction, she is blissfully incapable of getting from point A to point B without a guide, turning every simple journey into an accidental detour through the wilderness.

Tyde was found lost in the sewers of [location:9418490|Waterdeep] while searching for nature. After being spotted by [organisation:9419162|the party], she joined their ranks. She assisted the group in rescuing [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar] from the clutches of [character:9432251|Nihiloor] and [character:9432250|Grum’shar] within a [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] hideout. During the skirmish, she managed to scramble out of the path of a [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] before the party defeated it. She is now a member of [organisation:9419162|the party] and a resident of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor].

Recently, Tyde has begun expanding her ties with local factions. She was invited to join the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave] after a speaking cat approached her and [character:9425235|Alyzira]. She is particularly eager to work with the Enclave to locate her missing group of coastal druids. She was formally granted membership by [character:9435919|Jeryth Phaulkon] at [location:9435917|Phaulkonmere Villa], where she received a [item:9435948|charm of restoration] and a promise of assistance in finding her lost kin. Additionally, Tyde recently attended an opera at the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater] in a sparkly silver-and-blue gown to maintain the party's social standing and investigate leads for the [organisation:9419383|Harpers].

Tyde recently assisted the party in investigating reports of living scarecrows terrorizing the [location:9437517] on Undercliff Way. For her role in defeating the scarecrows and saving the farmlands, she was awarded 20 Gold Pieces and gained +1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave]. During a patrol of the [location:9438979] (the local cemetery) on behalf of the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], she was struck by a devastating spell and died temporarily, but was quickly revived by [character:9423629]. Following the capture of a priest, she earned an additional 10 gold pieces and +1 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave].

During an infiltration of [location:9443309], Tyde wildshaped into a wolf to help the party dispatch five [organisation:9419438] swordsmen. She also utilized her ability to wildshape into a spider to bypass a barricaded door in the same villa, allowing the group to discover Lord [character:9443311|Orond Gralhund].

Most recently, Tyde used her animal handling skills to earn the trust of [character:9443969|Bonesnapper], a young griffon. She utilized the mount to perform an aerial search of the [location:9418606|Dock Ward] to track a missing automaton, coordinating with the party from the skies. During this hunt, she used her tracking device to help corner a rogue nimblewright in the [location:9435900]. Following the battle, Tyde was rewarded with 100 gold pieces and a backpack parachute that negates fall damage.

Tyde has continued her service to the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], recently engaging in combat against a pack of wererats from the [organisation:9453215] in Endshift Alley. She also participated in a successful hunt for a rogue grell in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward], an operation that earned her an additional +2 Renown with the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave] and a [item:9435948|charm of heroism].

Trollskull Manor is a historic, formerly abandoned townhouse and tavern located in [location:9419015] within [location:9418490]’s [location:9431893|North Ward]. Once a lively neighborhood tavern known as the “Trollskull,” the building fell into disrepair after a tragic fire and years of neglect, becoming a decaying but character-filled ruin with a distinctive troll skull mounted on its roof. In its modern state, it has been reclaimed and restored by adventurers, transforming it into a functional base of operations, tavern, and gathering place for allies, contacts, and faction agents.

Construction on [location:9418605] is officially finished, and the inn is now fully open for business. While the manor remains inhabited by its resident poltergeist, “Leif” (Lif), the property has transitioned from a renovation project into a completed establishment. The property was recently acquired by [organisation:9419162|the party] from [character:9418259|Volothamp Geddarm].

Recent developments include reports from [character:9443960|Istrid] regarding two suspicious halfling applicants who visited the porch seeking employment. Following a confrontation in Endshift Alley, the party highly suspects these individuals are wererats from the [organisation:9453215] attempting to infiltrate the manor. Additionally, the party's rival, [character:9438945|Emmek Frewn], has been spotted lurking around the tavern.

Laeral Silverhand is the current Open Lord of [location:9418490], a legendary archmage and former adventurer who now governs the City of Splendors with a rare blend of wisdom, restraint, and immense magical authority. As one of the famed Silverhand sisters and a Chosen of Mystra, she is deeply connected to the weave of magic itself, and her long life has given her both the patience to navigate Waterdeep’s complex politics and the resolve to act decisively when the city is threatened.

Unlike more authoritarian rulers, Laeral tends to favor delegation through trusted institutions like the Lords of Waterdeep, the City Watch, and allied factions, intervening personally only when the stakes are truly dire. She remains a stabilizing force in a city perpetually balanced between order and chaos.

Recently, she personally intervened regarding the theft of the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr]. The Dock Ward of [location:9418490] is the rough, bustling heart of the city’s working waterfront, where sailors, dockworkers, fishmongers, merchants, and smugglers all collide in a constant churn of commerce and chaos. It is one of the most densely packed and colorful districts in Waterdeep, filled with creaking warehouses, leaning tenements, noisy taverns, and narrow streets that smell of saltwater, tar, and spilled ale. Ships from across the [location:9418394] and beyond crowd its piers, bringing goods, rumors, and trouble in equal measure.

Recent activity has seen a fleet of ships belonging to the Sea Maidens Faire carnival, owned by [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord], docking at the ward's piers. This includes the galleons Heartbreaker and Hellraiser, while their flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher], remains anchored in Deepwater Harbor. The area has also recently been a site of monster hunting, with adventurers successfully eliminating a pair of grells that were terrorizing the district.

While officially under the protection of the City Watch, the Dock Ward is notoriously difficult to police completely, and many of its darker dealings are quietly influenced by criminal factions and dockside power brokers. Despite its grime and danger, it is also a place of opportunity, where fortunes can be made quickly—and lost even faster. "If you want to understand Waterdeep, don’t start in the palace halls or noble villas—start at the docks. Everything that enters the city passes through here, and so does everything the city would rather forget."

While officially under the protection of the City Watch, the Dock Ward is notoriously difficult to police completely, and many of its darker dealings are quietly influenced by criminal factions and dockside power brokers. Despite its grime and danger, it is also a place of opportunity, where fortunes can be made quickly—and lost even faster. Originally serving as the city's deepwater naval harbor, it degraded over the decades into a polluted morass where the unwanted, outcasts, and criminals sought refuge among beached, rotting hulks and interconnected, half-sunken ships. The area is defined by its constant, heavy ocean fog, rank-smelling waters, and a landscape scarred by a massive fire that left portions of the makeshift neighborhood in charred ruins—leaving roofless dens now occupied by rats, urchins, and desperate bandits loitering on the decks of tenements like the Kraken’s Folly. It remains a hazardous fringe of the City of Splendors where the City Watch actively avoids entering unless forced to do so at double strength with weapons drawn, making it the ultimate hideout for those looking to vanish completely into the shadows.

Laeral Silverhand is the current Open Lord of [location:9418490], a legendary archmage and former adventurer who now governs the City of Splendors with a rare blend of wisdom, restraint, and immense magical authority. As one of the famed Silverhand sisters and a Chosen of Mystra, she is deeply connected to the weave of magic itself, and her long life has given her both the patience to navigate Waterdeep’s complex politics and the resolve to act decisively when the city is threatened.

Unlike more authoritarian rulers, Laeral tends to favor delegation through trusted institutions like the Lords of Waterdeep, the City Watch, and allied factions, intervening personally only when the stakes are truly dire. She remains a stabilizing force in a city perpetually balanced between order and chaos.

Recently, she requested the party's assistance in retrieving the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] from a secret cellar complex in the [location:9435916|South Ward]. However, upon retrieving the artifact, it was discovered to be a counterfeit—a common stone painted to mimic the real object. Following this setback, the party intends to consult with "Laeral" at the [location:9453223|Seven Masks Theater] in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward].

[character:9423629|Orlum] is a gray-green tortle paladin who cuts an imposing figure with his tall stature and immense, heavy build. Bound by holy oaths, he possesses a remarkably straightforward and earnest mind, though his social interactions are often marked by a charming quirk: he takes whatever people say entirely literally, often missing figures of speech or sarcasm completely. Despite his formidable presence and martial devotion, [character:9423629|Orlum] harbors a gentle appreciation for sweet simple comforts. This is best exemplified by his absolute favorite possession—a magical pumpkin cupcake that miraculously replenishes itself, ensuring he is never without his preferred treat.

Following advice from [character:9418614|Laerel Silverhand], Orlum and his allies infiltrated the [location:9435916|South Ward] sewers to locate a hidden [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] outpost. During the infiltration, Orlum took the lead by feeling along the sewer walls to reveal secret doors. He also successfully activated a mechanical beholder device found within the complex, which emitted colorful beams of light. After clearing several chambers and defeating various creatures, including troglodytes and a gibbering mouther, Orlum used his brute strength to smash open a locked chest containing a hoard of coins, a gold beholder pendant, and a spell scroll. Upon returning to [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], the party discovered that the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] they had retrieved was actually a counterfeit; Orlum discovered this by licking the stone and finding it tasted of wet paint.

Recently, Orlum traveled to the [location:9431892|Castle Ward] courthouse to meet with Magister [character:9491072|Hester Barch]. Leveraging his reputable standing in the [organisation:9419404|Order of the Gauntlet], he helped convince the Magister to grant his party an audience with the prisoner [character:9445748|Fenerus Stormcastle]. After being discovered by the Magister and subsequently arrested, Orlum and his allies used an Earthquake spell to escape. During a subsequent investigation at a dead-magic tower in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward], Orlum scavenged clean swords from the floor, though he later faced a brief struggle when those same swords animated as Flying Swords during a rooftop chase.

previous_entry: Renaer is the estranged son of [character:9457192|Dagult Neverember], the former Open Lord of Waterdeep and the current Lord of Neverwinter. Father and son detest one another. Renaer is least happy when he finds himself forced to deal with some mess his father left behind. Qualities that both share include striking good looks, a love of drink, and a flair for diplomacy. What Renaer lacks is his father's belligerence, ill temper, and bad judgment. Renaer lives off a sizable inheritance left to him by his mother, Alethea Brandath. Approaching middle age, he has given up adventuring and "settled down" somewhat. As a member of the [organisation:9419383], he spends a lot of time defending Waterdavians against those who, like his father, would deprive them of their coin and rights. He owns [location:9443317|Brandarthall], a four-story residence in the [location:9431883]. Renaer spends as little time there as possible, however, since it's constantly under surveillance by spies loyal to his father. His friends have an open invitation to use the house as they please, while Renaer spends most of his free time in taverns and festhalls. Some believe that Renaer's estrangement from his father is nothing but an act, and that anyone who bears the Neverember name is an enemy of [location:9418490]. Renaer just shakes his head at such accusations and gets on with his life. He has many powerful friends to watch his back. Recently, Renaer was kidnapped by [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] thugs who were searching for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] in connection to alleged embezzlement by his father. Renaer is the estranged son of [character:9457192|Dagult Neverember], the former Open Lord of Waterdeep and the current Lord of Neverwinter. Father and son detest one another. Renaer is least happy when he finds himself forced to deal with some mess his father left behind. 

 Qualities that both share include striking good looks, a love of drink, and a flair for diplomacy. What Renaer lacks is his father's belligerence, ill temper, and bad judgment. 

 Renaer lives off a sizable inheritance left to him by his mother, Alethea Brandath. Approaching middle age, he has given up adventuring and "settled down" somewhat. As a member of the [organisation:9419383], he spends a lot of time defending Waterdavians against those who, like his father, would deprive them of their coin and rights. 

 He owns [location:9443317|Brandarthall], a four-story residence in the [location:9431883]. Renaer spends as little time there as possible, however, since it's constantly under surveillance by spies loyal to his father. His friends have an open invitation to use the house as they please, while Renaer spends most of his free time in taverns and festhalls. 

 Some believe that Renaer's estrangement from his father is nothing but an act, and that anyone who bears the Neverember name is an enemy of [location:9418490]. Renaer just shakes his head at such accusations and gets on with his life. He has many powerful friends to watch his back.  

 Recently, Renaer was kidnapped by [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] thugs who were searching for the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] in connection to alleged embezzlement by his father. As the wealthiest ward of the city, Sea Ward is the seat of power for the established noble houses. Nearly empty during the winter due to the fierce sea storms, many of the nobles, well-to-do merchants, and social climbers call this home in the summer. Walking along the Street of the Singing Dolphin, the major avenue for the ward, one can expect to spot many of the grandest homes in [location:9418490], from the spires and gables of noble villas to the craggy and mysterious turrets of the wizards' towers. Sea Ward also contains many of the city's temples and Heroes' Garden, the only public garden outside the [location:9438979|City of the Dead]. Truly important (and self-important) people come to this ward to build their opulent homes while more modest folk or those more entrenched in the everyday politics and power of the city often choose to live in [location:9431892].

As with [location:9431893], watch patrols are quite frequent as one of the benefits of position. They are always polite and generally lightly armed, as most of the miscreants they find in this ward are well-dressed, drunken nobles who need only to be steered to the next party. The Watch deals swiftly with any other disruptions, their tolerance for any vandalism, violence, or theft being quite low. The boundaries for this district are Julthoon Street and Shield Street, with a small eastern arm extending to the High road along Vondil Street. The ward is symbolized by blue-and-gold colors and a sea lion mascot.

[character:9425235|Alyzira Galanodel] is a half-elf bard who carries herself with a slender yet athletic build. Strikingly charming and inherently charismatic, she naturally steps forward as the eloquent, persuasive "face" of her adventuring party during high-stakes negotiations and social maneuvers. Her true passion lies in performance—where her sharp wits and musical talents shine beautifully in private or casual settings. However, [character:9425235|Alyzira] harbors a hilarious and deeply ironic curse: the moment a formal audience gathers to watch her perform, her standard bardic grace utterly vanishes, transforming her otherwise masterful art into a brilliantly comedic disaster.

Recently, following advice from Open Lord [character:9418614|Laerel Silverhand], [character:9425235|Alyzira] and her party infiltrated a hidden [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] outpost within the [location:9435916|South Ward] sewers. During that mission, she used magic to enchant [character:9425236|Eoula] with flame arrows and cast bear's endurance to bolster her during a fight against troglodytes. The party successfully retrieved what they believed to be the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], but upon returning to [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], it was discovered that the artifact was merely an ordinary rock cleverly painted to look magical.

Seeking guidance on the stone, the party visited [character:9456996|Rongquan Mystere] at the [location:9453223|Seven Masks Theater], who provided a lead regarding the bandit [character:9445748|Fenerus Stormcastle]. During a subsequent attempt to visit a courthouse in the [location:9431892|Castle Ward], [character:9425235|Alyzira] successfully bribed a clerk for an audience with Magister [character:9491072|Hester Barch]. However, after being caught in a lie regarding their true intentions, she and her companions were forced to flee the courthouse amidst a massive prison break.

Following the interrogation of [character:9445748|Fenerus], which involved [character:9425235|Alyzira] using detect thoughts to locate the real [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], the party traveled to a dead-magic tower in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward]. During a rooftop chase through [location:9457007|Mistshore], she engaged fleeing drow gunslingers with her longbow. She has previously expanded her influence within the city through various successful maneuvers, assisting investigations involving the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim], the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], and the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild].

[character:9425236|Eoula] is a diminutive female halfling ranger of mature years, possessing an exceptionally light and delicate frame. Deeply intellectual, she harbors a profound love for books and reading, though this quiet studiousness leaves her horribly awkward and out of her element in social situations. In combat, she primarily trusts her shortbow, but she also delights in unleashing sticky webs from her prized spider staff—a choice of weaponry wrapped in deep irony, given her intense dislike of actual spiders. Above all, [character:9425236|Eoula] possesses a fiercely compassionate heart for animals, driven by a protective nature that simply cannot bear to see creatures of the wild come to any harm.

Following a meeting with [character:9456996|Rongquan Mystere] at the [location:9453223|Seven Masks Theater], which confirmed their previous artifact was a counterfeit, [organisation:9419162|the party] engaged in a chaotic heist at a courthouse in the [location:9431892|Castle Ward]. After escaping the custody of Magister [character:9491072|Hester Barch] following a massive prison break, the group interrogated the bandit [character:9445748|Fenerus Stormcastle]. During this interrogation, it was revealed that the authentic [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] is hidden within an abandoned tower in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward].

After securing [character:9445748|Fenerus], the group locked him safely inside a wardrobe under [character:9425236|Eoula]’s watch before investigating the rumored "Dead-Magic Tower." During their exploration of the tower, they encountered drow gunslingers and engaged in a high-stakes rooftop chase through [location:9418606|Dock Ward] and [location:9457007|Mistshore].

[character:9425238|Tyde Undertow] is a striking, fey-touched or tiefling-like druid whose appearance beautifully bridges the gap between the wild earth and the deep ocean with vibrant blue skin transitioning into soft pink and silver tones across their limbs. Though her favorite wildshape forms for a fierce battle are a predatory wolf or a snapping crocodile, [character:9425238|Tyde]'s greatest challenge isn't a formidable enemy, but a simple map. Possessing absolutely zero sense of direction, she is blissfully incapable of getting from point A to point B without a guide, turning every simple journey into an accidental detour through the wilderness.

[character:9425238|Tyde] was found lost in the sewers of [location:9418490|Waterdeep] while searching for nature. After being spotted by [organisation:9419162|the party], she joined their ranks. She assisted the group in rescuing [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar] from the clutches of [character:9432251|Nihiloor] and [character:9432250|Grum’shar] within a [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] hideout. During the skirmish, she managed to scramble out of the path of a [creature:9432254|Intellect Devourer] before the party defeated it. She is now a member of [organisation:9419162|the party] and a resident of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor].

Recently, Tyde has continued her service to the [organisation:9419386|Emerald Enclave], engaging in combat against wererats and hunting a rogue grell. During an infiltration of the [location:9435916|South Ward] sewers, she wildshaped into a wolf to help the party ambush duergars and a Gazer. Following that battle, the group retrieved what they believed to be the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], though it was later revealed at [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] to be a counterfeit painted rock.

During a heist at a courthouse in the [location:9431892|Castle Ward], Tyde wildshaped into an alligator to create a massive distraction, baiting guards into opening a gate. This allowed her allies to slip into the cell blocks unnoticed. Later, during a rooftop chase through the [location:9457007|Mistshore] district to pursue fleeing drow gunslingers, she used *Misty Step* to maintain the high ground. Most recently, after escaping an anti-magic tower in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward], Tyde successfully cast *locate object* to lock onto the true position of the authentic [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr].

Gralhund Villa rises behind twelve-foot stone walls in [location:9418490]’s [location:9431893], an imposing noble estate that projects wealth, power, and secrecy in equal measure. Ornate iron gates open onto manicured grounds dotted with flowering trees and winding paths that lead to a grand two-story mansion of polished brick and dark timber. Inside, soaring ceilings, crystal chandeliers, rich mahogany furnishings, family portraits, and lavish tapestries speak to generations of prosperity.

Though outwardly the home of Lady [character:9443310|Yalah Gralhund] and Lord [character:9443311|Orond Gralhund], the villa has recently been a site of violent chaos. Following a raid by the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim], the estate's ground floor shows signs of significant bloodshed, including the deaths of the butler and a halfling cook. The conflict was partially triggered by a nimblewright automaton equipped with a necklace of fireballs, which accidentally caught members of the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] in a blast while attempting to retrieve the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr].

Lady [character:9443310|Yalah Gralhund] has since provided conflicting accounts to the City Watch regarding the incident. She claimed that [character:9443308|Urstul Floxin] and his [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] agents held her family hostage for ten days following the fireball explosion, and that Lord [character:9443311|Orond Gralhund] fought them off. She further alleged that a nimblewright delivered to the villa was actually a rogue spy that stole her necklace.

Investigations within the villa revealed that the Gralhunds have been secretly bankrolling [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] operations, with funding provided by the agent [character:9443960|Istrid Horn]. The estate also contains a guest room featuring a teleportation circle and evidence of a struggle involving [character:9443308|Urstul Floxin], who had been staying there before turning on the family.

The Dock Ward of [location:9418490] is the rough, bustling heart of the city’s working waterfront, where sailors, dockworkers, fishmongers, merchants, and smugglers all collide in a constant churn of commerce and chaos. It is one of the most densely packed and colorful districts in Waterdeep, filled with creaking warehouses, leaning tenements, noisy taverns, and narrow streets that smell of saltwater, tar, and spilled ale. Ships from across the [location:9418394] and beyond crowd its piers, bringing goods, rumors, and trouble in equal measure.

Recent activity has seen a fleet of ships belonging to the Sea Maidens Faire carnival, owned by [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord], docking at the ward's piers. This includes the galleons Heartbreaker and Hellraiser, while their flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher], remains anchored in Deepwater Harbor. The area has also recently been a site of monster hunting, with adventurers successfully eliminating a pair of grells that were terrorizing the district.

The ward is home to a crumbling, local tower enveloped in a powerful magic ward that renders all spells and cantrips useless; superstitious residents avoid this structure due to rumors of hauntings. Additionally, the nearby run-down dockside neighborhood of [location:9457007|Mistshore] serves as a desolate area where recent skirmishes with drow gunslingers have taken place.

While officially under the protection of the City Watch, the Dock Ward is notoriously difficult to police completely, and many of its darker dealings are quietly influenced by criminal factions and dockside power brokers. Despite its grime and danger, it is also a place of opportunity, where fortunes can be made quickly—and lost even faster. "If you want to understand Waterdeep, don’t start in the palace halls or noble villas—start at the docks. Everything that enters the city passes through here, and so does everything the city would rather forget."

Tucked away along the northernmost stretch of [entity:9418490|Waterdeep]’s squalid [location:9418606], Mistshore is a destitute and lawless shantytown known as a "riotous assemblage of ramshackle homes". Originally serving as the city's deepwater naval harbor, it degraded over the decades into a polluted morass where the unwanted, outcasts, and criminals sought refuge among beached, rotting hulks and interconnected, half-sunken ships.

Waterdeep —often called the City of Splendors—is one of the largest, richest, and most influential cities in the Forgotten Realms, a sprawling coastal metropolis where nobles, merchants, adventurers, and criminals all compete for power under a carefully balanced system of open governance and hidden influence. Ruled by the mysterious Lords of Waterdeep and publicly represented by the Open Lord, the city thrives on trade, magic, and politics, drawing in wealth and danger from across [location:9418260] through its vast harbor and strategic position on the [location:9418394]. Beneath its grand estates, bustling wards, and famed institutions lies a labyrinth of secrets: ancient ruins, hidden guild operations, and conspiracies that can shape the fate of nations.

The city's various wards, such as the [location:9431892|Castle Ward], the shadow-filled [location:9418606|Dock Ward], the [location:9435916|South Ward], and the parkland cemetery known as the [location:9438979|City of the Dead], serve as backdrops for intense factional violence between groups like the [character:9419465|Xanathar] Guild and the Zhentarim. Recent disturbances include wererat muggings in the [location:9453202] within the [location:9438959|Field Ward], and a violent raid on the home of [character:9445748|Fenerus Stormcastle] in the Trades Ward, which left behind the bloody mark of the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild].

Recent events have centered around the recovery of a massive treasure hoard from a corrupted windmill in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward]. This vault, once guarded by the ancient gold dragon [character:9461667|Aurinax] (formerly known as [character:9461667|Barok Clanghammer]) on behalf of the disgraced former Open Lord Neverember, was successfully accessed by adventurers. The hoard is intended to be returned to benefit the people of [location:9418490|Waterdeep], though the machinations of [character:9443318|Jarlaxle] suggest the city's wealth remains a central piece in a much larger game of deception.

It is one of the most densely packed and colorful districts in Waterdeep, filled with creaking warehouses, leaning tenements, noisy taverns, and narrow streets that smell of saltwater, tar, and spilled ale. Ships from across the [location:9418394] and beyond crowd its piers, bringing goods, rumors, and trouble in equal measure.

Recent activity has seen a fleet of ships belonging to the Sea Maidens Faire carnival, owned by [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord], docking at the ward's piers. This includes the galleons Heartbreaker and Hellraiser, while their flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher], remains anchored in Deepwater Harbor. The area has also recently been a site of monster hunting, with adventurers successfully eliminating a pair of grells that were terrorizing the district.

The ward is home to a crumbling, local tower enveloped in a powerful magic ward that renders all spells and cantrips useless; superstitious residents avoid this structure due to rumors of hauntings. Additionally, the nearby run-down dockside neighborhood of [location:9457007|Mistshore] serves as a desolate area where recent skirmishes with drow gunslingers have taken place. In Mistshore, adventurers recently tracked the true [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] to a beached ship known as the [location:9491271|Kraken's Folly].

It is one of the most densely packed and colorful districts in Waterdeep, filled with creaking warehouses, leaning tenements, noisy taverns, and narrow streets that smell of saltwater, tar, and spilled ale.

Ships from across the [location:9418394] and beyond crowd its piers, bringing goods, rumors, and trouble in equal measure. Recent activity has seen a fleet of ships belonging to the Sea Maidens Faire carnival, owned by [character:9443973|Zardoz Zord], docking at the ward's piers. This includes the galleons Heartbreaker and Hellraiser, while their flagship, the [location:9443986|Eyecatcher], remains anchored in Deepwater Harbor.

The area has also been a site of monster hunting, with adventurers successfully eliminating a pair of grells that were terrorizing the district. The ward is home to a crumbling, local tower enveloped in a powerful magic ward that renders all spells and cantrips useless; superstitious residents avoid this structure due to rumors of hauntings.

previous_entry:
A local [location:9418490|Waterdeep] butcher and friend of [character:9423618|Gladio], Raucous joined the party at the [location:9431699|Yawning Portal] amidst a tavern brawl and a monster outbreak from the central well. He has been acting as a guide for the group, leading them through the [location:9418606|Dock Ward] in their search for [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar]. During an investigation of a [location:9437421|Zhentarim Warehouse] in the [location:9431893|North Ward], Raucous accidentally triggered an alarm while exploring the upper level, which drew the attention of the City Watch. Raucous recently led the party in a successful rescue of [character:9431741|Floon Blagmaar] from a [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] hideout in the sewers. During the skirmish, he looted a spellbook from the body of a half-orc named [character:9432250|Grum’shar]. Following the rescue, Raucous took the lead in escorting [character:9431741|Floon] back to the [location:9431699|Yawning Portal] to reunite with [character:918259|Volothamp Geddarm]. The party subsequently acquired the deed to [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] in [location:9419015|Trollskull Alley] as payment for the rescue.

Raucous was recently recruited into the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] by [character:9435899|Mirt] "the Merciless" after attending an opera at the [location:9435901|Lightsinger Theater]. He was tasked with locating a talking draft horse mare named [character:9435910|Maxeene], who serves as a spy for the faction. After the horse was located, Raucous received a sealed envelope containing 100 gp and 1 Renown with the [organisation:9419383|Harpers] as a reward for his service. Recently, Raucous has been involved in the party's efforts to fund the renovations of [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor] and prepare for the upcoming [event:9438944]. He participated in a mission to the [location:9438958] in the [location:9438959] to break up a gang war between rival thugs on behalf of the [organisation:9419404]. Most recently, he was part of the group that investigated a necromantic threat in the [location:9438979] at the request of the [organisation:9419386], resulting in the capture of Priest [character:9442159]. During a chaotic battle against the [organisation:9419438|Zhentarim] at [location:9443309|Gralhund Villa], Raucous untied the Zhentarim member [character:9443308|Urstul Floxin]. In the same encounter, he expertly pickpocketed [character:9443311|Lord Orond Gralhund], stealing 50 gold pieces and a strange compass. Later, while investigating a lead regarding the "[character:9443961|Black Viper]", Raucous smoothly pickpocketed [character:9443962|Gaxly Rudderbust], stealing back 30 gold pieces that had been used as a bribe.

Following the completion of construction on [location:9418605|Trollskull Manor], Raucous has continued performing faction-related tasks. He recently participated in an investigation at [location:9453202] in Endshift Alley to address muggings by a gang of wererats known as the "[organisation:9453215]"; during the ensuing confrontation, he successfully pickpocketed the combatants while they were distracted. He also assisted the party in hunting grells in the [location:9418606|Dock Ward] at the request of the [organisation:9419386]. During a heist at a courthouse in the [location:9431892|Castle Ward], Raucous used mimicry to distract guards, allowing him to pick the locks on every cell door and trigger a massive prison break. Following the chaos, he successfully delivered the bandit [character:9445748|Fenerus Stormcastle] back to the party.

While investigating a dead-magic tower, Raucous engaged in a high-stakes rooftop chase through the [location:9418606|Dock Ward] and [location:9457007|Mistshore], pursuing fleeing drow gunslingers. During a subsequent confrontation at a beached ship in [location:9457007|Mistshore], Raucous used the assistance of [character:9425238|Tyde] to sneak up on the drow gunslingers Fel’rekt Lafeen and Krebbyg Masq’il’yr, successfully pickpocketing them for gunpowder, a [item:9432044|Tankard of Sobriety], and an oval stone.

Raucous has since identified and attuned to the true [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr], discovering it is actually an ancient Aboleth. This attunement has cursed him with blindness if he moves more than 10 feet away from the stone, though it allows him to cast *Legend Lore* three times a day. While investigating a lead in the [location:9431883|Sea Ward], Raucous used his keen eyes to locate a hidden stone trapdoor beneath the residence of [character:9457182|Kalain], which led the party to the entrance of the Vault of Dragons.

Jarlaxle Baenre is a brilliant, charismatic drow rogue and mercenary leader. Rather than possessing innate shape-changing magic, he is a master of disguise who relies on a vast collection of magical items to constantly alter his appearance, deceive foes, and run his spy networks.

previous_entry:
Laeral Silverhand is the current Open Lord of [location:9418490], a legendary archmage and former adventurer who now governs the City of Splendors with a rare blend of wisdom, restraint, and immense magical authority. As one of the famed Silverhand sisters and a Chosen of Mystra, she is deeply connected to the weave of magic itself, and her long life has given her both the patience to navigate Waterdeep’s complex politics and the resolve to act decisively when the city is threatened.

Unlike more authoritarian rulers, Laeral tends to favor delegation through trusted institutions like the Lords of Waterdeep, the City Watch, and allied factions, intervening personally only when the stakes are truly dire. She remains a stabilizing force in a city perpetually balanced between order and chaos.

Recently, she requested the party's assistance in retrieving the [item:9432044|Stone of Golorr] from a secret cellar complex in the [location:9435916|South Ward]. However, upon retrieving the artifact, it was discovered to be a counterfeit—a common stone painted to mimic the real object. Following this setback, the party sought guidance at the [location:9453223|Seven Masks Theater], where [character:9456996|Rongquan Mystere]—who claims to answer directly to Laeral—confirmed the counterfeit nature of the stone and provided a new lead regarding the true location of the artifact.

previous_entry:
With no distinct look to separate it from surrounding wards, Trades Ward is somewhat lost in terms of neighborhood identity. On the other hand, though it lacks in neighborhood "feel," its sense of community in commerce occupies nearly every building and person within the entire ward. Many of [location:9418490]'s middle class and merchant class live and work here.

The busiest of wards due to all the constant commercial work within its boundaries, Trades Ward is active day and night, requiring excessive streetlights (many merchants say that Trades Ward at night is beautiful, "when her streets are filled with the stars of Waukeen"). The Guild of Chandlers and Lamplighters keeps a triple shift here at all times of the night, its streets filled with the bobbing lanterns of young lamplighters; the only more frequent sights in Trades Ward at night are the large and frequent watch patrols. While cursing, shoving, and minor street tussles are typical behavior within this business district, the worst criminal offenses are theft, vandalism, and destruction of private property - the watch patrols are more often needed to protect thieves from angry merchants than to stop robberies!

The ward boundaries are defined by the city walls and the [location:9438979|City of the Dead] on the east, and Andamaar's Street to the High Road on the north. The High Road and Snail Street border it on the west until Shesstra's Street cuts east to the Way of the Dragon where it links with the northern boundary of Southern Ward. Due to its central nature and rambling boundaries, it is hard to traverse the city without passing through this ward at some point.

The ward's commercial nature is further complicated by the presence of organized crime and the city's sprawling sewer system. While the streets are patrolled by the City Watch, the subterranean tunnels beneath the ward serve as a labyrinthine territory for various factions, including the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild]. Recent events in the ward's alleyways include a violent ransacking of the home of [character:9445748|Fenerus Stormcastle], where the [organisation:9419437|Xanathar Guild] left their mark in blood.
